source.author: verg
source.text: Nate, meae vires, mea magna potentia solus, nate, patris summi qui tela Typhoia temnis, ad te confugio et supplex tua numina posco.
source.text_original: 'Nate, meae vires, mea magna potentia solus, / nate, patris summi qui tela Typhoia temnis, / ad te confugio et supplex tua numina posco.
source.text_english: My son, my strength, my great power, you alone, my son, who scorn the Typhoean weapons of the highest father, to you I flee, and as a suppliant I ask for your divine aid.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: quasi non legerimus Homerocentonas et Uergiliocentonas ac non sic etiam Maronem sine Christo possimus dicere Christianum, quia scripserit: iam redit et uirgo, redeunt Saturnia regna, iam noua progenies caelo demittitur alto, et patrem loquentem ad filium: nate, meae uires, mea magna potentia solus, et post uerba saluatoris in cruce: talia perstabat memorans fixusque manebat.
reuse.text_original: quasi non legerimus Homerocentonas et Uergiliocentonas ac non sic etiam Maronem sine Christo possimus dicere Christianum, quia scripserit: iam redit et uirgo, redeunt Saturnia regna, iam noua progenies caelo demittitur alto, et patrem loquentem ad filium: nate, meae uires, mea magna potentia solus, et post uerba saluatoris in cruce: talia perstabat memorans fixusque manebat.
reuse.text_english: as if we had not read the Homerocentons and the Vergiliocentons, and as if we could not in this way call even Maro a Christian without Christ, because he wrote: now the virgin returns, Saturn’s reign returns, now a new race is sent down from high heaven, and the father speaking to the son: son, my strength, my great power, my only one, and after the Savior’s words on the cross: he kept standing thus as he remembered, and remained fixed there.
